topicName: Verification vs. Validation & Quality Assurance vs. Quality Control
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Verification vs. Validation & Quality Assurance vs. Quality Control in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the realm of manual software testing, understanding foundational concepts is crucial for building robust applications. Four terms that are frequently confused, yet distinct in their purpose, are Verification, Validation, Quality Assurance (QA), and Quality Control (QC). This tutorial breaks down these concepts with practical examples tailored for manual testers."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Verification vs. Validation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both verification and validation are processes used to check if a software product meets its specifications, but they operate at different stages and answer different questions."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Verification (Are we building the product right?)"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Definition: The process of evaluating work products (not the final product) to determine whether they meet the specified requirements and conditions."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Focus: Process-oriented. It checks documents, design, code, and architecture."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Manual Testing Activities: Requirements walkthroughs, design reviews, code inspections, and test plan reviews."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Validation (Are we building the right product?)"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Definition: The process of evaluating the final software product during or at the end of development to determine whether it satisfies user needs and requirements."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Focus: Product-oriented. It deals with the actual working software."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Manual Testing Activities: Functional testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), exploratory testing, and usability testing."},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"2. Quality Assurance (QA) vs. Quality Control (QC)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"While QA and QC are both part of quality management, they focus on different aspects of the software development lifecycle: process versus product."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Quality Assurance (QA)"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Definition: A set of activities designed to ensure that the development process is adequate to yield a system that meets quality requirements."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Proactive process. It aims to prevent defects before they happen."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examples: Defining standard operating procedures (SOPs), conducting process audits, and setting up coding guidelines."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Quality Control (QC)"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Definition: A set of activities used to evaluate a developed product to ensure it contains no defects and meets the specified requirements."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope: Reactive process. It aims to identify and fix defects in the final product."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Examples: Executing manual test cases, logging bugs in a defect tracking tool (like Jira), and verifying bug fixes."},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"3. Practical Manual Testing Scenario"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a manual testing team working on a new e-commerce checkout page. How do these four concepts apply?"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Verification: The QA lead reviews the functional requirements document to ensure the discount code field validation rules are clearly documented before development starts."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Validation: A manual tester opens the deployed checkout page, enters an invalid discount code, and checks if the correct error message displays as expected by the user."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Quality Assurance (QA): The team establishes a peer-review policy for all test case creation to ensure high coverage."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Quality Control (QC): The tester executes the checkout test suite, uncovers a payment gateway crash, and logs a defect ticket."},{"order":29,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering the distinctions between verification, validation, QA, and QC empowers manual testers to contribute effectively across the entire software development lifecycle, ensuring both process excellence and product reliability."}]
